Bug_Title: Regex boundaries should not be used in a way that can never be matched
Bug_Details:
In regular expressions the boundaries ^ and \A can only match at the beginning of the input (or, in case of ^ in combination with the MULTILINE flag, the beginning of the line) and $ , \Z and \z only at the end.
These patterns can be misused, by accidentally switching ^ and $ for example, to create a pattern that can never
match.
Noncompliant code example
// This can never match because $ and ^ have been switched around
Pattern.compile("$[a-z]+^"); // Noncompliant
Compliant solution
Pattern.compile("^[a-z]+$");
Bug_Explanation: The bug occurs because the regex pattern uses boundaries '$' and '^' incorrectly by placing them in positions that can never match. '$' is meant to signify the end of a string or line, and '^' signifies the start. Swapping their positions in a pattern like '$[a-z]+^' makes it impossible for any input to match.

The method attempts to use a regex pattern that has incorrect boundaries '$[a-z]+^', which can never match any input. As a result, the matcher.find() will always return false, and the method will return 'No match found', making the test case fail when it expects 'Match found: exampletext'.
